rationale: Round 0 compiled and passed, so I am raising obfuscation aggression while staying restrained on the hot search core: Pathfinder spends most of its runtime in findAndLogAllPossibleLeg and the node/vector traversal loops in searchAlgorithms.c and vectorUtils.c, so BCF and FLA get high SecurityGain/DiversityGain but only moderate RuntimeCost weight (0.4-0.5) to bias the selector away from wrapping tight loops in bogus control flow; SPLIT is the cheapest and safest transform, so it keeps the highest RuntimeCost/SizeCost tolerance (0.7/0.6) and can apply broadly, including to the big parsing functions (parseFile, parseConfigFile, main) where flattening plus splitting gives the best structural confusion per byte; IBR gets high DiversityGain (0.8) since basic-block relocation composes well with FLA and adds layout diversity at modest cost; SUB is enabled broadly with a low CorrectnessRisk weight (0.1) because arithmetic substitution in this integer/bitfield-heavy code is cheap and safe; ICALL and IGV keep slightly higher CorrectnessRisk weights (0.3) since indirect calls and global-variable hiding touch linkage and initializer semantics in a program with many cross-file tables (systemCallMap, configuration), but both remain enabled because round 0 showed the build tolerates the pipeline and they meaningfully raise static-analysis effort on the parsing and configuration layers that dominate the text size.
